importantConcepts: Definition and significance of Triple Point.
notes: **Definition.** The triple point of a substance is the single temperature and pressure at which its solid, liquid and vapour phases coexist in stable equilibrium.
**Water's triple point.** For water it occurs at 273.16 K (0.01 °C) and 611.73 Pa (about 4.58 mmHg) — the fixed reference point of the Kelvin temperature scale.
**Phase diagram.** On a pressure–temperature diagram the triple point is where the melting, boiling and sublimation curves meet; below its pressure a solid sublimes instead of melting.
**Per-substance value.** Each pure substance has its own triple point (for CO₂ it is −56.6 °C at 5.1 atm), so the value identifies the substance's phase behaviour.
**Thermometric use.** Because it is reproducible and substance-specific, the triple point of water is used to calibrate precision thermometers.
